name: Wuzhi capsule
short: Raises blood levels of the immunosuppressant tacrolimus (meta-analysis of 11 studies). In transplant and myasthenia gravis studies, adverse reactions were no more common with the capsule.
text: Wuzhi capsule is described in the cited abstracts as an extract (in one, an ethanol extract) of Schisandra sphenanthera (Nan-Wuweizi). Its main documented interaction is with tacrolimus, a prescribed immunosuppressant: a meta-analysis of 11 studies (6 randomized trials and 5 observational studies) found whole-blood tacrolimus levels significantly higher with the capsule than without, and a study in healthy volunteers found that the capsule decreased the apparent oral clearance of tacrolimus. The meta-analysis notes that in China the capsule is usually prescribed to raise tacrolimus levels. On safety, the meta-analysis found the capsule generally well tolerated, with no significant difference in the incidence of adverse reactions between groups; a retrospective study of 194 kidney transplant recipients found no significant differences in blood counts, liver or kidney function, or adverse reactions; and in a retrospective study of 122 adults with myasthenia gravis taking tacrolimus, 14 (11.5%) reported adverse drug reactions, and their incidence was not related to taking the capsule. The two patient studies were retrospective, and the abstracts do not list the specific adverse reactions.
